STEP 1 - Vessel type: The plate is a flat, square white plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall, so it is a square flat plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size: Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large, about 25 cm across. The plate fills about 450 px of the 640 px frame, and the fork-free edge gives no further scale, so I use 25 cm (625 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items (footprint from visible coverage, thickness by eye, grams = footprint x thickness x density):
- Cottage cheese (curds): about 35% of the plate, 219 cm². Average thickness about 1 cm, so 219 ml x 1.0 = about 220 g.
- Salsa verde (tomatillo sauce): a mound on the cheese, about 12% of the plate, 75 cm². Average thickness about 0.8 cm, so 60 ml x 1.0 = about 60 g.
- Roasted sweet potato cubes: about 12%, 75 cm². Average thickness about 2 cm, so 150 ml x 0.6 = about 90 g.
- Watermelon cubes: about 13%, 81 cm². Average thickness about 2 cm, so 162 ml x 0.6 = about 97 g.

Total is about 467 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No separate base layer is visible beneath the toppings. The cheese acts as the base, and it is already counted.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served): cottage cheese about 100, salsa verde about 35, roasted sweet potato about 120 (with some oil), watermelon about 30. Totals: cheese about 220 kcal, salsa about 21, sweet potato about 108, watermelon about 29, so roughly 380 kcal in total.
